summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, diabetes, and prior MSSA abscess was admitted for new bilateral leg swelling and exertional shortness of breath. The swelling began two days prior and was associated with a 20-pound weight gain, coinciding with an increase in gabapentin dose six days earlier. Workup revealed no pulmonary embolism, DVT, heart failure, or infection. The rash on his thighs was determined to be benign folliculitis, not vasculitis or cellulitis. Gabapentin was reduced to the prior dose, Lasix was given for fluid management, and compression stockings were started. Symptoms improved during the stay. He was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
